today_summary: GCM26 marked $4,156.7 with ATM IV 21.14%, implying a $55.4 (1.33%) 1σ daily move. Put walls sit at $3,500 (6,464 OI), $4,000 (4,654) and $3,900 (4,067); call walls at $5,000 (12,384), $4,500 (9,908) and $4,725 (9,546), with P/C OI 0.39 on 238,788 calls against 94,042 puts. Net GEX within ±$200 of spot is −233.7 and the gamma flip strike sits $698 higher at $4,855, so every strike in the tradeable range is short-gamma. Session flow was the thinnest of the window — 5,877 call lots and 2,054 put lots, concentrated in the $5,000 call (864) and $4,850 call (855), both more than $690 out of the money.
five_day_thesis: Spot net −$22.9 over five sessions (4,179.6 → 4,156.7) but the path matters more than the number: a $45.5 advance into the 4,202.2 high on 10/02, then two straight down days that gave all of it back — a failed breakout, not a downtrend. The structural change is upside OI migrating toward spot: far-OTM calls unwound hard ($8,000 −3,864, $6,000 −3,272) while the $4,700–$5,100 band built ($5,100 +2,973, $4,850 +1,073, $4,700 +760), dragging the call wall from $6,000 to $5,500 and compressing the resistance shelf closer to price. The put floor never moved — $3,500 pinned all five sessions and added 358 contracts to 6,464 — so the chain is tightening from above, not firming from below. Gamma is the risk: net GEX ±$200 deepened from −223.8 to −233.7 while the flip strike drifted up $55 to $4,855, widening the spot-to-flip short-gamma pocket from $620 to $698. IV compressed 21.80% → 21.14% (−0.66pp) into a 75% collapse in call volume (23,620 → 5,877) — dealers are short gamma into a market that has stopped transacting, the setup where a single real bid or offer travels.

prediction: Bias neutral-to-bearish below $4,175, where the nearest call shelf (833 OI) caps the failed-breakout retest. Short gamma through the entire range plus 75% lower volume means moves extend rather than mean-revert — expect the 1σ $55 range to be exceeded on any headline, with the first real downside shelf not until the $4,050 put (2,450 OI). Reclaiming $4,202 (the 10/02 high) invalidates the bearish read and opens the thin air to the $4,500 call wall.
